analysis.title: The Index Is A Lie, AI Is Holding The Tape; Top Goldman Trader Warns Midterms 'Probably Won't Be Risk Positive'
key_insights: Goldman's Louis Miller (global head of equity custom baskets) says growth is getting scarcer, so the composition of growth matters more. The market is likely to favor compounders with durable growth over high-growth cyclicals, which face slowing momentum from higher rates, elevated oil and rising energy costs.

De-escalation-driven investment narratives are harder to underwrite with the Fed still tightening, oil near $100 and 10-year yields above 5%. GS's call on AI over cyclicals (SPXXAI Index) has worked and it still likes it.
Miller says the midterms 'probably won't be risk positive'.

Softer PCE and NFP prints helped the market push out the next Fed hike. Europe exposure feels increasingly uncomfortable as fiscal risk builds. Japan is the standout in Asia, with a $140bn AI datacenter push.

Index-level equities keep grinding higher through the rates selloff, but the AI trade is holding the market up. Rate-sensitive pockets are under pressure: US Homebuilders (GSXUBLDR) -17.5% over 3 months, Non-Profitable Tech (GSXUNPTC) -11.4% since early July. Lending Sensitive Equities (GSXULEND) have underperformed, and Regional Banks (GSCBRGBK) have been more resilient relative to their rates beta and could have downside if rates stay elevated.

Softer PCE and NFP are pushing yields lower, which could drive significant relief in rate-sensitive pockets if sustained. Weak breadth implies scope for a broader beta rally, expressed via the sector/industry-neutral beta basket (GSPUBETA). The Beta-ex-AI pair (GSPUBETX) has underperformed GSPUBETA with consistently high correlation, and GS recommends it as a hedge for cautious investors.

Power fundamentals remain intact. GS research sees 108 GW of datacenter power demand by 2030 (23% CAGR off a 2025 base) and a 3.5% CAGR in total US power demand, of which datacenters contribute just over 2.5% (1.8pp front-of-the-meter, 0.8pp behind-the-meter). GEV is guiding to 125 GW of backlog plus slot reservation agreements by year end, roughly 6x current capacity.

Power valuations have de-rated: IPPs are down ~30% over 12 months and gas infrastructure names are down ~13% over 3 months. Behind-the-meter generation is expected to be ~20% of datacenter power demand by 2030, driven by a 4.5-year interconnection queue and state-level permitting friction. Catalysts: FERC ruling on the PJM large-load framework, 3Q earnings, November midterms, ERCOT datacenter interconnection audit. GS likes owning upside into year-end via Power Up America (GSX1POW1), which has lagged other AI themes YTD.
GS launched an Asia Battery Backup Units basket (GSXABBUS) covering batteries, modules and energy storage systems. GS research expects the global BBU TAM to expand 23x between 2025 and 2030E.

French OAT-Bund spreads are around 150bps with signs of contagion into BTPs this week, so the market is pricing broader European sovereign risk. European Banks (SX7E) were hit hard after an 18-month rally and heavy net length.

If French fiscal risk stays contained, GS would buy dips in EU Banks on a solid structural earnings outlook, but is cautious on stocks with weak balance sheets and upcoming debt maturities (GSXECLFF). The European Domestic vs US exposed pair (GSPEDOAM) has historically been most reactive to EURUSD.

Japan AI (GSXAJPAI) is breaking out from the broader Asia AI Datacenters basket (GSXADATA), supported by AI leadership, gradual BoJ normalization and a less hawkish BoJ summary of opinions. Flows have increasingly favored Japan AI over EM AI. GS's favorite Japan AI trade is the Optical Networking basket (GSXAJONE).

China consumer: Golden Week data is the key watch when China reopens next week. Another disappointing print would reinforce concerns that stimulus is incremental. GS economists see a widening production-consumption gap from a structural pivot to high-tech manufacturing, negative for employment, household income and consumption.

GS likes shorts on Asia Consumer Inertia stocks (GSXASWCH). China consumer sentiment needs to inflect for EU Luxury (GSXELUXG) to work, though low valuation and stable EPS momentum have raised interest ahead of mid-month 3Q updates.

Brazil first-round elections are this weekend. GS flags Brazil Rate Sensitive (GSBZRATE) as the key equity trade. A Bolsonaro win would be bullish for equities, and rate-sensitive equities could re-rate up to 30% in a 200bp rate cut outcome.

The ZeroHedge commentary frames the market as two discount rates in one: AI capex is underwritten as if power, batteries and fiber are the new duration, while everything else bears the cost of capital with the 10-year above 5% and oil near $100.
